items.note: First sentence begins with 'Produces', not 'Returns', so per the stated rule the `@return` tag should have been kept, but it was dropped. This does mirror the pre-existing (out-of-diff) trait-level `newArray` doc at line 58, which uses the same 'Produces ... no @return' style, so it's consistent with the file's existing convention even though it technically diverges from the literal drop-@return rule.

The doc phrases the cache-disable condition as an ongoing toggle ('unless caching is turned off by setting the system property ... to true'), but `cacheDisabled` (line 131) is a `private val` read once at object initialization via `java.lang.Boolean.getBoolean`. Setting the property after the `ClassTag` object is initialized has no effect. Minor precision issue, not misleading about the documented method's actual runtime behavior once initialized.

'the JVM's descriptor form' is a slightly imprecise/jargon-y way to describe what `Class.getName()` returns for array types (e.g. `[Ljava.lang.String;`), which isn't quite the JVM's formal descriptor syntax (that uses `/` as package separator). The intent is clear and not factually wrong, just a bit cryptic for a reader unfamiliar with class-file internals.
